newsitem.title: UK: UK GILTS BRUSH ASIDE CBI SURVEY, FOCUS ON RATES.
newsitem.headline: UK GILTS BRUSH ASIDE CBI SURVEY, FOCUS ON RATES.

text.p: UK gilt futures were fractionally weaker in sluggish early trade as dealers marked time before the announcement of the Bank of England's decision on whether to change interest rates, due at 1100 GMT.

"There's really not a lot happening. We're sitting on our hands until midday (1100 GMT)," one senior gilt salesman said. "People really aren't sure what the Bank is going to do but I think they'd be better off raising rates again today and then they could leave it for a while."

British official rates stand at 6.75 percent after a 1/4 point increase in each of the past three months. Last week the view was that a rate rise was firmly on the agenda but the decision is now viewed as more finely balanced.
By 0718 GMT, LIFFE September gilts had recovered to Wednesday's closing levels and were unchanged at 114-21/32.
"We feel that on balance there is not enough economic evidence to support a further rate hike," said Royal Bank of Scotland economist Neil Parker.
He said GDP growth has now been 0.9 percent for Q1 and Q2 1997, slightly slower than in Q4 1996 and that whilst retail sales were strong, they did not accelerate in June.

Meanwhile M4, which has achieved renewed prominence because of the central bank's new interest rate setting powers, has seen monthly growth slow to below the recent average although the annual growth rate of 11.7 percent is at a six and a half year high.
LIFFE September short sterling is almost discounting official rates of 7.25 percent but has been backing off in recent days. It was up three basis point at 92.75 by 0750 GMT.
The contract suggests UK rates will peak at around 7.5 percent and then remain little changed for the rest of the century.

Bunds were weak again giving gilts the chance to take the spread back below 150 basis points -- Wednesday's closing level. It was 148 basis points this morning and dealers say it has scope to narrow further if the central bank leaves rates alone today.
The international focus is on the final leg of the U.S.'s quarterly refunding programme. It will auction 10 billion dollars of 30-year U.S. Treasuries at 1745 GMT.
